ordered_diagnoses: Gastric cancer with lymph node metastasis

candidates.name: Gastric cancer with peritoneal metastasis
support_spans: A 72-year-old man with a history of stage IIIA gastric cancer treated by distal gastrectomy and adjuvant S-1 six months previously developed peritoneal and para-aortic lymph-node recurrence
candidates.why: The patient has a history of gastric cancer with peritoneal metastasis, which is a common site for gastric cancer to spread.

candidates.name: Febrile neutropenia
support_spans: He was treated for febrile neutropenia with G-CSF: his neutrophil count and fever improved within three days
candidates.why: The patient was diagnosed with febrile neutropenia, which is a common complication of chemotherapy.

candidates.name: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH)
support_spans: Fluid intake was restricted to 1 L/day for presumed SIADH, but the hyponatremia persisted
candidates.why: The patient was diagnosed with SIADH, which is a common cause of hyponatremia in cancer patients.

candidates.name: Cachexia
support_spans: He experienced progressive anorexia and general fatigue and was referred for further evaluation
candidates.why: The patient has symptoms of cachexia, which is a common complication of advanced cancer.
